objectives: Name the big parts of a kitchen.
Say what the plates, bowls, spoons and forks are for.
Tell which food goes in the fridge and which goes in the cupboard.
Use the new kitchen words in a sentence.
Help with a small kitchen job from start to finish.
Stay safe around hot pans and sharp knives.

sections.body:
A kitchen is the room where we make food and eat it. It has water, heat and lots of useful things.

Every kitchen has the same big parts. There is a place to cook. There is a place to keep food cold. There is a place to keep food dry. There is a sink for washing things, and a table where the family sits.

In Vietnam the rice cooker often stands on the counter. Many families also have a gas stove, a microwave, and a big pot for soup. The fridge keeps food cold. The cupboard holds the bowls and the glasses.

Now look around your own kitchen. You will find things you use every day, like a spoon. You will also find things you use only sometimes, like a cake tin or a jar of spices.

The kitchen is a busy room. If you know the names of the things in it, you can ask for what you need and help at home.
examples: This is the kitchen, where we cook and eat.
The rice cooker is on the counter.
I wash my hands at the sink.
sections.heading: What a kitchen is, and why we need it

sections.body:
A **plate** is flat and wide. We put rice and fried food on a plate.

A **bowl** is deeper than a plate. It holds soup, or cereal, or rice porridge. In Vietnam we often eat from a bowl with a spoon and chopsticks.

A **spoon** is for soup and soft food. A **fork** is for food in small pieces. A **chopstick** is a thin stick, and we hold two of them together. A **glass** is for water and juice.

Some tools are only for cooking. A **knife** cuts things, and it is for grown-ups. A **peeler** takes the skin off a carrot. A **grater** makes cheese into small bits.

There are tools for drinking too. A **cup** is bigger than a glass, and we drink tea from a cup.

Put every tool back where you found it. A tidy kitchen is easier to cook in.
examples: The soup is too hot for the baby, so I use the small bowl.
I need a spoon for the rice porridge.
This fork is for the meat.
sections.heading: The things we eat with

sections.body:
Every kind of food has its own home in the kitchen.

The **fridge** keeps cold things cold. Milk, meat, eggs and leftover food go inside it. The **freezer** keeps things frozen for a long time. Ice cream stays there until someone wants it.

The **cupboard** is for dry food. Rice, flour, sugar and noodles stay on the shelf. Dry food does not need a fridge.

The **counter** is the flat top where you prepare food. You chop vegetables there. The **kettle** boils water for tea. The **rice cooker** cooks rice by itself, and it clicks when the rice is ready.

Some food belongs to everybody. Some food belongs to one person only. A small bowl on a high shelf might be for your little brother. Ask before you eat it.
examples: The milk goes in the fridge.
The noodles stay in the cupboard.
The rice cooker clicks, so the rice is ready.
sections.heading: Where the food lives in the kitchen

sections.body:
These are the words you will hear in the kitchen. Learn them and you can ask for what you need.

A **spoon** is a small bowl with a handle. We use it for soup and rice.

A **fork** has a handle and sharp points. We use it for food with small pieces.

A **bowl** is a deep round dish. Soup and cereal go in a bowl.

A **fridge** is the white cold box in the kitchen. It keeps food fresh for a day or two.

A **cupboard** is a tall box with doors. Dry food and clean dishes live inside it.

These five words will take you a long way. Add a word like please, and people will know exactly what you mean.
examples: The spoon is in the drawer.
I put the milk back in the fridge.
Where do you keep the bowls? In the cupboard.

sections.body:
Helping in the kitchen is a set of small jobs. Do them in the same order and they are easy to remember.

Start with your hands. Wash them with soap and water, and dry them well.

Next, get what you need. Take the bowls, the spoons and the plates out of the cupboard.

Then set the table. Put a plate at each place. Put a spoon beside it. Put a glass on the right side.

After the meal, clear the table. Carry the dishes to the sink gently. Hot things you use two hands for.

Last, wash and put away. Put clean plates back in the cupboard, and wipe the table with a cloth.

Do not touch the stove while it is hot. If a job is too hard for you, ask an adult to do it.
examples: The soup bowl is hot, so I use two hands.
sections.heading: How to help in the kitchen
steps: Wash your hands with soap and water.
Take the bowls, spoons and plates from the cupboard.
Set one plate, one spoon and one glass at each place.
Carry the dishes to the sink after the meal.
Wash, dry and put the clean dishes away.

sections.body:
The kitchen has hot things and sharp things in it. A few rules keep everyone safe.

Never touch a pot that is on the stove. Steam can burn you, and you cannot see it clearly. Use a towel for a hot lid, and ask an adult to help with hot water.

Knives are for grown-ups. If you want to cut a fruit, ask someone to cut it for you.

Keep your fingers away from the top of the blender and the food grinder while it is running. Switch it off before you put anything in.

Do not climb on a chair to reach the top cupboard. Ask an adult to get it down for you.

And if you spill water on the floor, wipe it up at once. A wet floor is a slip.
examples: The pot is hot, so I ask my mother for help.
I do not use the knife by myself.
I wipe the water on the floor.
sections.heading: Staying safe in the kitchen

item.summary: The kitchen is the busiest room in the house. After reading this, you can name the things you find in a kitchen, say what each one is for, and help safely while the family cooks.
item.title: Things We Find in the Kitchen
